newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in range trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in range trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late Monday trading, dealers said.
They said trading was in a narrow range, with operators seen expecting increased rupiah supply on Tuesday.
One Japanese bank dealer said there was some anticipation of ample supply because many operators had bought one-week short-term papers (SBIs) last Tuesday.

However, interbank rates were stable, with overnight money last traded at 13.0 percent. Some dealers said ample supply might also be compensated due to the weekly tax payments and the approaching festivities in early February.
Spot rupiah was at 2,370.25/71.00 at 0945 GMT against an opening of 2,370.25/71.25. Tomorrow closed at 2,369.90/70.50.
There was no trading in value today because of a public holiday in the United States on Monday.
One dealer said earlier that operators could not go short heavily because the dollar was now traded at the lower end of the floor rate.
He said operators could not go long too much either because rupiah liquidity was a bit unsteady and the Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr festivals were approaching.

The Lunar New Year celebration will be due on February 7 and Eid al-Fitr on February 9 and 10. One-month swaps were at 11.50/11.75, two at 22.5/24.00, three at 33.00/34.00 and six at 72.00/72.50 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,368.0/2.560 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,368/2,416 on Monday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week.
